# Causal analysis (Phase 7, RQ3)

*Generated by `python -m src.causal.causal_report` from `data/processed/causal/`. Do not edit by hand. Rules: the registered plan (`docs/analysis_plan.md` at `6e24eca`, https://osf.io/jksne/) §5, read as in DEC-135; every gap filled before any estimate in DEC-138 to DEC-150 (commit `eebaecc`, pushed before computing). Estimates: listed minus counterfactual on log concentration; negative = a reduction; % = 100 × (e^β − 1).*

**Parts A and B are complete:** Layer A (satellite PM2.5, H1/H2), Layer B (ground), triangulation, every sensitivity check, and one exploratory check added after seeing H1 (§11).

## 1. H1 (confirmatory, primary): the registered decision

> **H1** (registered): NCAP enrolment reduced annual population-weighted PM2.5 in enrolled urban centres, relative to comparable non-enrolled centres, 2019–2024 (2020 excluded).
>
> **Verdict: not identified by this design (failed: (b) pre-trend Wald test).**
>
> NCAP units' satellite PM2.5 did not fall relative to comparable units; the estimates point to a relative rise of about 3–5%. H1 is not identified by this design, so this is not an effect of NCAP.

**Every rule, as registered (plan §5) and read in DEC-135/141.** The verdict takes the first branch that applies: (b) or (c) failing → not identified; else a reduction with a CI excluding 0 → supported if (d) holds; an increase → not supported; a CI including 0 → no detectable effect, with the equivalence test.

| rule | value | met |
|---|---|---|
| (a) primary SDID ATT < 0 and its 95% CI entirely below 0 | ATT +0.0352 (+3.6%); 95% CI +0.0238 to +0.0465 (+2.4% to +4.8%) | **no** |
| (b) event-study pre-period coefficients −9 … −2 jointly insignificant (Wald p > 0.10) | χ² = 26.79, df = 8, p = 0.0008 | **no** |
| (c) the 2016 placebo-in-time 95% CI includes 0 | -0.0011; 95% CI -0.0093 to +0.0070 | yes |
| (d) point estimate < 0 in Callaway & Sant'Anna, area-weighted and V6.GL.03 | Callaway & Sant'Anna +0.0447; area-weighted +0.0346; V6.GL.03 +0.0314 | **no** |

**Reported whatever the outcome:**
- 90% CI: +0.0256 to +0.0447 (+2.6% to +4.6%); it is within the equivalence bounds ln 0.95 = -0.0513 to ln 1.05 = +0.0488, so effects of 5% or more in either direction are ruled out at the 5% level (reported for information: the verdict is decided by the branch above).
- The 95% CI's lower bound is +0.0238 (+2.4%); against NCAP's targets it excludes a 20% reduction; excludes a 30% reduction; excludes a 40% reduction. NCAP's targets (20–30%, later up to 40%) were set for **PM10**; a satellite PM2.5 result says nothing directly about PM10 attainment.
- MDE (Phase 4, a best-case lower bound): 0.0117 in log units (1.2% fall). The SE of the real design is 0.0058, i.e. 2.8 × SE = 0.0162 (1.6%).
- Placebo in space: the primary ATT against the 500 joint-placebo aggregates, equal-tailed permutation p = 0.004 (the minimum possible): no placebo set of control centres moved as much.
- Calibration-leakage warning sign (§3): **yes**: the difference (gained minus not gained) is negative with a CI excluding 0.

## 3. Calibration leakage (pre-specified, beside H1)

ACAG calibrates satellite PM2.5 to ground monitors, and NCAP added monitors mainly in treated cities. The primary design is re-estimated separately for treated units that gained a CAAQMS station inside their polygon with first PM data in 2019–2024 and for those that did not (DEC-096/146); SEs from the same joint-placebo replications.

| specification | estimate (log) | estimate (%) | 95% CI (%) | SE (log) | permutation p |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Gained a monitor 2019–2024 (74 units) | +0.0249 | +2.5% | +1.1% to +4.0% | 0.0073 | 0.004 (the minimum possible) |
| Did not (39 units) | +0.0535 | +5.5% | +3.5% to +7.5% | 0.0096 | 0.004 (the minimum possible) |
| Difference, gained − not gained | -0.0287 | -2.8% | -5.1% to -0.5% | 0.0123 | 0.020 |

**Warning sign of leakage (registered rule): YES — the difference (gained minus not gained) is negative with a CI excluding 0.** It is a warning, not proof: units that gained monitors also differ in size and pollution.

*Read with the signs:* both groups' estimates are increases (+2.5% and +5.5%); the group that gained monitors rose less. The rule was written with reductions in mind and fires here on its second clause. The direction is the one calibration leakage would produce (ACAG calibrated to new monitors that, per Phase 6, read cleaner than existing ones would pull the satellite values of those units down), but the comparison cannot separate that from real differences between the two groups.

**A possible mechanism the design cannot test.** Phases 3 and 6 found that new CAAQMS stations read cleaner than the existing stations of the same city and year: PM2.5 -5.8% in Phase 3 (raw), and in Phase 6 -6.3% raw (95% CI -11.7 to -0.3) and -6.8% deweathered (-12.4 to -0.9): the gap is about where the new monitors stand, not the weather. If ACAG's calibration absorbed those cleaner readings, the satellite values of the units that gained monitors would be pulled down, which is the direction of the difference above. This design cannot test it: the calibration inputs are not observed here, and the two groups also differ in size and pollution. The V6.GL.02.04 vintage, calibrated to an earlier monitor set, is the registered related check (§9).

## 11. Exploratory, added after seeing H1: overlapping ranges of 2015 population (DEC-155)

*Not a decision rule; it cannot change the H1 verdict.* City size was the largest pre-registration imbalance (log-population SMD 1.44). Variant (i), min–max common support, drops the megacity units and the sub-100,000 towns but does not improve balance, because the control pool is concentrated at 100,000–200,000. Variant (ii) keeps the overlap of the 5–95% ranges, which halves the imbalance. Both use the primary design otherwise, with joint-placebo SEs from their own pools.

| sample | treated | controls | log-population SMD | estimate (log) | estimate (%) | 95% CI (%) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Primary: V5.GL.06, population-weighted, listing cohorts, never-treated controls, 2020 dropped | 113 | 923 | 1.44 | +0.0352 | +3.6% | +2.4% to +4.8% |
| Exploratory: min-max common support of 2015 population | 98 | 923 | 1.63 | +0.0365 | +3.7% | +2.5% to +5.0% |
| Exploratory: overlap of the 5-95% ranges of 2015 population | 42 | 704 | 0.91 | +0.0298 | +3.0% | +1.2% to +4.9% |

## Caveats that travel with every Layer A number

- The MDE is a best-case lower bound (plan §3); the confidence intervals use the real design's joint-placebo SE.
- ACAG is calibrated to ground monitors (§3 is the pre-specified check; the V6.GL.02.04 vintage comparison is in Part B).
- Satellite PM2.5 says nothing directly about PM10, NCAP's target pollutant.
- Had it been identified, the design would estimate the effect of being listed, relative to comparable centres; it could not say which city action worked.
- Figure 4: `reports/figures/fig4_event_study.{png,svg}`.
